known_tbc_divergences.name: hook-yield abandon drops final closer error
known_tbc_divergences.description: When a debug-hook yield abandons C frames above the hook frame, their TBC chain entries are closed non-yieldable with err=null; the FINAL closer error is dropped (PUC closes these entries later at the parent poscall with the eventual error; the hook-yield abandon has no error to thread). VM error state is snapshotted around the closes so a closer error does not leak into the suspended thread's resume state.

known_tbc_divergences.name: close-context wrong thread (builtinCoroutineClose close_has_err)
known_tbc_divergences.description: A thread that died with an in-flight C call may carry TBC chain entries on parked C frames; coroutine.close closes them with the thread's error (non-yieldable, last-error-wins, mirroring PUC luaE_resetthread/luaD_closeprotected), but the closers run in the CLOSING thread's context instead of the closed thread's stack. Observable only via coroutine.running() inside __close during a dead thread's cleanup.

known_tbc_divergences.name: unwindBytecodeExecFrames void path swallows close errors
known_tbc_divergences.description: The void-returning abort fallback (frame construction/dispatch aborted before a semantic unwind could start) closes popped C frames' TBC entries non-yieldable with err=null and swallows closer errors/yields via catch {} — no error can propagate from a void errdefer path. Normal runtime/OOM propagation and yielding __close continuations go through continueBytecodeErrorUnwind instead.
